findings.body:
**The ai-sdk isolation note omits the bound-workspace case.**

When an invocation has no `sessionRef` but carries a `workspace` binding, the ai-sdk driver creates the fresh session record inside the bound workspace, not in a new temporary workspace. The README line 141-142 states that no `sessionRef` always gives a fresh temp workspace. Update the README to describe both cases.
findings.title: The ai-sdk isolation note omits the bound-workspace case.

findings.body:
**Document the correlation variables as an exception to the no-`CQ_*` rule.**

The README states that nothing `CQ_*` reaches a worker. The default-deny allowlist does block inherited `CQ_*` variables. An invocation that carries `correlation` still receives explicitly stamped values. `applyCorrelationEnv` writes `CQ_WORK_ID` and `CQ_RUN_ID` into the child environment, along with the other correlation names. The claude-code CLI, SDK, and ACP transports all call it. Name this exception in the paragraph so that operators do not draw the wrong conclusion.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-`SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, and `NODE_OPTIONS`/`NODE_PATH` — and nothing `CQ_*` ever
-reaches a worker (the sandbox policy knobs are launcher-side only). Per-
+`SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, and `NODE_OPTIONS`/`NODE_PATH` — and no inherited `CQ_*`
+variable reaches a worker (the sandbox policy knobs are launcher-side only).
+The explicit exception is session correlation: when an invocation carries
+`correlation`, `applyCorrelationEnv` (`src/driver/correlation-env.ts`) stamps
+`CQ_WORK_ID`, `CQ_RUN_ID`, and the other correlation names into the child
+environment. Per-
```
